title: Email Privacy & Encryption Privacy Hardening Checklist
metaDescription: Complete checklist to secure your email with encryption, privacy-focused providers, and best practices for anonymous communications.
intro: Email is one of the most vulnerable forms of digital communication. This comprehensive checklist will help you secure your email communications with encryption, switch to privacy-focused providers, and implement best practices to protect your personal information from surveillance and data breaches.

items.task: Switch to a privacy-focused email provider
items.why: Traditional email providers like Gmail and Yahoo scan emails for advertising and may share data with third parties or government agencies.
items.howTo: Sign up for ProtonMail, Tutanota, or Fastmail. These providers offer end-to-end encryption, are based in privacy-friendly jurisdictions, and don't scan your emails for ads.

items.task: Create a strong, unique password for your email account
items.why: Your email is often the recovery method for other accounts, making it a high-value target for attackers.
items.howTo: Use a password manager to generate a unique 16+ character password with mixed case, numbers, and symbols. Never reuse this password elsewhere.

items.why: 2FA adds an extra security layer, protecting your account even if your password is compromised.
items.howTo: In your email provider's security settings, enable 2FA using an authenticator app like Authy or hardware security key rather than SMS.

items.task: Set up secure account recovery options
items.why: Insecure recovery methods can be exploited by attackers to gain access to your account.
items.howTo: Remove phone numbers as recovery options. Use a secondary encrypted email address or write down recovery codes and store them securely offline.

items.task: Set up PGP encryption for sensitive communications
items.why: Even with secure providers, additional encryption ensures only intended recipients can read your messages.
items.howTo: Generate a PGP key pair using tools like GPG or your email client's built-in encryption. Share your public key with contacts and always verify their keys before use.

items.task: Use email aliases for different purposes
items.why: Aliases help compartmentalize your digital identity and make it harder to track your activities across services.
items.howTo: Create separate aliases for shopping, social media, work, and personal use. Many secure providers offer unlimited aliases or use services like AnonAddy.

items.task: Disable automatic image and content loading
items.why: External images and content can contain tracking pixels that reveal when and where you open emails.
items.howTo: In your email client settings, turn off automatic image loading and HTML content. Review emails in plain text when possible.

items.why: Many email clients collect data about your usage patterns and may have security vulnerabilities.
items.howTo: Use clients like Thunderbird with privacy extensions, or your secure provider's web interface through Incognito Browser for better privacy protection.

items.task: Always verify recipient addresses before sending sensitive information
items.why: Typos in email addresses can send sensitive information to unintended recipients, and attackers may use similar addresses to deceive you.
items.howTo: Double-check email addresses, especially for sensitive communications. Be wary of slight variations in familiar addresses that could indicate spoofing attempts.

items.task: Avoid sending highly sensitive information via email
items.why: Email is inherently less secure than dedicated encrypted messaging platforms, even with encryption enabled.
items.howTo: For highly sensitive communications, use Signal or other encrypted messaging apps. If you must use email, use PGP encryption and consider self-destructing messages.

items.task: Regularly delete old emails and empty trash
items.why: Old emails contain personal information that can be valuable to attackers and increase your exposure if your account is compromised.
items.howTo: Set up automatic deletion of emails older than 1-2 years. Regularly empty your trash and sent folders. Archive important emails locally if needed.

items.why: Email is the primary vector for phishing attacks that can compromise your accounts and steal personal information.
items.howTo: Never click links in unexpected emails. Verify sender authenticity through other channels. Check URLs carefully and use Incognito Browser to safely investigate suspicious links.
